findings.title: Empty attribute list is left as literal text instead of being removed
findings.evidence:
The issue asks for `

Title

`, `

Some paragraph

` and `

hi

`. At the PR head, `python -c "import markdown; ..."` prints: '# Title {: }' -> '

Title {: }

'; 'Some paragraph\n{:}' -> '

Some paragraph\n{:}

'; '*hi*{: }' -> '

hi{: }

'. Adding `:` to the excluded first characters in BASE_RE stops the regex from matching an empty list at all, so the `{: }` text stays in the rendered page. That page is still wrong for the reporter's template. A fix should match the empty list, remove it, and add no attributes. For example, let the capture group be empty and skip assignment when nothing is parsed.

findings.title: Tests only check that ` :>` is absent and would pass with the wrong output
findings.evidence:
`assertNotIn(' :>', html)` passes for '

Title {: }

', which is not the output the issue expects. The tests should use `assertMarkdownRenders` with the exact output (`

Title

`, `

Some paragraph

`, `

hi

`). They should also cover the inline case from the issue, which has no test now. They also skip the repo's TestCase helpers and import markdown inside the method.

notes: Side effect: lists whose first token starts with ':' (e.g. `*hi*{ :foo }`) used to become an attribute `:foo` and are now left as literal text. That change probably doesn't matter in practice, but it is outside the issue's scope.
The changelog entry is in place, but it has a stray blank line between it and the next bullet, unlike the rest of the list.
Non-empty lists still work: `{: .note }`, `{:.note}` and `{: #id }` give the expected output. The full suite passes: 1168 tests, OK (skipped=52).

own_checks.check: Behaviour outside scope: leading ':' token (base vs head)
own_checks.command: monkeypatched base BASE_RE vs head on '*hi*{ :foo }'

summary:
The PR gets rid of the bogus `:` attribute by making BASE_RE stop matching empty lists. Because of that, `{: }` and `{:}` now stay in the output as literal text (`

Title {: }

`) when the issue expects them removed (`

Title

`). None of the three expected outputs in the issue are produced. The new tests only check that ` :>` is absent, so they pass with this wrong output.
